claims.text: Superconductivity in the Nb–Ti–Zr–Hf–Ta HEA is governed predominantly by electron-phonon coupling strength.
The electron-phonon coupling strength in this alloy is modulated by the density of states at the Fermi level.
Partial substitution of Ti with V changes the valence electron concentration.
Partial substitution of Ti with V shifts the density of states at the Fermi level.
The DOS shift caused by V substitution modifies the superconducting transition temperature.
The initial Nb–Ti–Zr–Hf–Ta alloy is an as-cast, homogeneous, single-phase bcc material with controlled grain size.
The relevant bcc Nb–Ti–Zr–Hf–Ta superconducting phase is close to a weak-coupling, phonon-mediated BCS superconductor.
Increasing the DOS at the Fermi level strengthens electron-phonon coupling and enhances Tc, whereas decreasing it lowers Tc.
Across the V-substituted series, samples with higher measured or computed Fermi-level DOS will have higher Tc than the V-free baseline.
The proposed DOS–Tc relationship applies only while the alloy remains single-phase bcc and relevant microstructural features remain unchanged.
Secondary phases or significant disorder induced above a critical substitution level may invalidate the DOS–Tc correlation.
Inadvertent local disorder or phase impurities may independently influence superconductivity.
Failure of Tc changes to correlate with measured DOS shifts under otherwise controlled structural and microstructural conditions would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.

contradictions.description: The boundary and uncertainty fields treat secondary phases or microstructural changes as confounders that invalidate application of the DOS–Tc relationship, whereas the falsification rule says that identifying such variations would itself falsify the mechanism. A confounded sample would normally make the test inconclusive rather than falsify the hypothesis.
